text:
maya: Nightly perf alert — p99 token latency jumped ~35% for medium-batch workloads after last night's release. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/nightdash/alerts/17825 :eyes:
ci-bot: nightly-perf-checker: alert triggered for channel eng-runtime (p99 increase). job: nightly-evictions-17825. link: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/nightly-perf/17825 :rotating_light:
sam: saw it. any obvious culprit? last deploy included PR #4823 (kernel-selector heuristics) and a batching tweak that landed at 02:13 UTC.
jorge: grabbing flamegraphs now. initial profile shows unexpected CPU time in attention kernels at seq=1024 for batch sizes 8-16. flamegraph gist: https://gist.github.com/jorge/ff12345
olga: FYI PR 4823 changed fallback order to prefer fused-attn for short seqs and adjusted batch alignment. suspect misprediction for medium seqs that forces suboptimal kernels. also seeing KV cache eviction spikes in logs.
kevin: starting a quick bisect on canary pool. will try reverting the batching alignment change first (commit a1b2c3).
kevin: bisect update — reverting commit a1b2c3 on canary drops p99 back to baseline. numbers: p99 210ms -> 155ms (medium-batch), throughput +4%. reproducible on staging. CI perf job earlier also showed regression: CI-789 failed metric thresholds.
maya: let's pause rollout for this release. @deploy-bot hold canary and stop further rollouts.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused for release v1.23.5. Reason: performance regression detected (p99 increase). Canary traffic frozen.
sam: quick reproducer for local testing: 
```
# run medium-batch perf test
./scripts/run_perf_test --model=gpt-medium --seq=1024 --batch=12 --iters=200  
# capture perf
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./build/bin/serve_perf --config test/configs/medium-batch.json
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
```
perf top excerpt from failing master:
```
45.1%  libattention.so  fused_attention_kernel
12.3%  libkernels.so    kv_cache_lookup
7.8%   libsched.so      schedule_work
```
jorge: KV cache metrics: miss_rate jumped from 2.1% -> 6.8% around deploy time, eviction_count +320% in 10m window. Possible cause: new batch alignment changes alter input chunking, generating more distinct cache keys. log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:21Z] KVCache: key_miss id=0x7fffa3 count=12
[2026-03-17T02:14:29Z] KVCache: evict id=0x9b2f reason=capacity
[2026-03-17T02:14:45Z] KVCache: miss_rate=6.8% window=60s
```
olga: I'm drafting a revert PR that removes the alignment change and restores previous kernel fallback. will add a regression test that runs the medium-batch profile nightly.
kevin: please include the CI perf job thresholds in the PR description and reference CI-789. also add a short smoke test to prevent this slipping through unit tests.
maya: good. also add a guard in kernel selector: if runtime seq distribution shows >20% at seq>=1024, prefer stable kernel until selector has more telemetry.
sam: opening follow-up issue to improve selector heuristics and telemetry (selector-accounting). will add a dashboard panel for seq distribution per route.
olga: created draft revert PR #4850 -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4850. tagging @kevin @maya for review.
kevin: reviewing now. if green I'll merge and trigger canary redeploy.
maya: after revert lands we'll re-run nightly perf and keep rollout paused until two consecutive nights show stable p99. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
